overview: A one-page list of papers for a 1940 State Department file concerning Japanese transportation regulations, specifically efforts by American President Lines to secure or facilitate licensing of a company automobile in Kobe. The register summarizes correspondence among the company, the Department, and the American Consulate at Kobe, including letters from company president William Gibbs McAdoo and Despatch No. 66 reporting negotiations over possible consular assistance.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the licensing of an American President Lines automobile in Kobe
subfiles.about: A file register summarizes correspondence and a consular despatch concerning attempts to facilitate the licensing of an American President Lines company automobile in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The list records an October 12 communication from American President Lines enclosing a letter from its president and requesting assistance with licensing a company car in Kobe. Subsequent October correspondence indicates that no arrangement could be made because the automobile lay outside the jurisdiction of the American Consulate at Kobe, and it records the forwarding of related letters dated October 12 and 13. A December 3 Kobe despatch, No. 66, reports negotiations concerning possible assistance with the automobile’s licensing; the list also notes its enclosure in correspondence dated January 1.

interest: This register is useful for reconstructing a correspondence sequence whose underlying letters and despatch may not be present in the surviving bundle. It illustrates the practical regulatory difficulties encountered by an American shipping company operating in wartime Japan and the limits imposed by consular jurisdiction. The chronology also points researchers toward Despatch No. 66 and the October 12–13 letters for fuller evidence about negotiations with Japanese licensing authorities.
